milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Requires approval-required MCP tools/call to match one Runtime-materialized, task-scoped approval fingerprint before server execution.
Allows autonomous task replay to reuse completed approved MCP evidence for the same request without duplicating tools/call.
Keeps MCP mutation-capable tool execution bounded by task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, annotation provenance, and Runtime approval evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement and headless_autonomous_development while preserving controlled_workspace_tools boundaries.
answers.new_capability: Runtime can execute approval-required MCP tools only when one concrete task-scoped approval fingerprint matches the exact tool request and pinned provenance.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: MCP-S2 and MCP-S3 left approval-required mutation-capable tools fail-closed; there was no Runtime-owned approval binding for a concrete tools/call request.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Mode Packs could describe approval-required MCP tools, but Brownie could not safely execute them or prove stale, broad, consumed, or mismatched approval evidence is rejected before server execution.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes Runtime MCP permission and execution behavior, ledger evidence, approval fingerprint matching, specs, and audits; it is not a wrapper, adapter manifest, new transport, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths are preserved; approval evidence is ledger-bound rather than CLI-owned authority.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates existing policy, execution evidence, specs, and audits rather than adding a summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Approval-required MCP tools deny before tools/call unless Runtime finds matching task/run/tool/request/catalog/annotation/safety-policy approval evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous runs can continue with approved MCP tools while deterministic replay avoids duplicate tools/call for the same completed invocation.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes MCP-S4 and leaves MCP-S5 through MCP-S7 open before Runtime Release Ready.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S4 changes Runtime MCP approval-required execution, so strict review must verify approval evidence is exact, task-scoped, bounded, and cannot widen Mode Pack policy or bypass annotation/catalog safety.

exit_criteria: Approval-required MCP tools/call execution requires one Runtime-materialized approval fingerprint before server execution.

Approval binding fingerprints cover task id, run id, normalized tool id, server id, tool name, request fingerprint, task-pinned catalog/schema/annotation provenance, server config identity, and structured Brownie MCP safety policy.
Missing, stale, consumed, malformed, mismatched, or over-broad approval evidence fails closed before tools/call.
Matching approval evidence permits the exact invocation and task-scoped replay does not duplicate tools/call.
Approval evidence cannot override Mode Pack allow-list, mcp_tool_access, legacy-unclassified/prohibited/destructive/unknown policy, annotation narrowing, or catalog drift.
MCP-S4 is marked closed while MCP-S5 through MCP-S7 and Runtime Release Ready remain open.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves approval-required MCP execution denies before tools/call without exact approval evidence.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves stale, consumed, and over-broad approval evidence fail closed before tools/call.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves matching runtime-ledgered approval evidence permits execution and repeated agent-loop handling does not duplicate tools/call.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records MCP-S4 as closed while leaving MCP-S5 through MCP-S7 open.

accepted_capability: Approval-required MCP tool calls are bound to concrete Runtime approval fingerprints.
Approved MCP execution remains task-pinned, provenance-bound, and replay-safe without duplicate tools/call.
behavior_evidence: Runtime focused MCP approval-binding test coverage proves exact approval matching, stale/consumed/broad denial, and no duplicate tools/call replay.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
Mode Pack structured policy remains the MCP tool safety authority; MCP annotations, descriptions, schemas, results, model output, and approval prose cannot grant authority.
Approval evidence only satisfies an additional Runtime gate for an already allowed server/tool/policy tuple; it cannot widen Mode Pack policy or bypass catalog and annotation drift checks.
non_goals: Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, public registry, automatic install, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
Does not close MCP-S5 through MCP-S7.
Does not close full CI workflow hardening while workflow update authority is unavailable.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected approval from CLI flags or model prose because caller text cannot grant Runtime authority.
Rejected broad server-level approval because approval must bind the exact task/run/tool/request/catalog/safety-policy tuple.
Rejected letting approval override annotation narrowing or catalog drift because server-supplied metadata is not authority and live provenance must still match task-pinned evidence.
technical_debt: MCP-S5 runtime input/output schema validation remains open.
MCP-S6 secret reference contract remains open.
Previously recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers remain open, including full CI workflow hardening.

runtime_release_dod: Runtime-owned MCP permission checks, tool execution, bounded evidence, replay, and completion semantics.
Task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, annotation provenance, approval provenance, and point-of-use Runtime safety enforcement.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths.
Existing ToolExecutionCompleted, ToolExecutionFailed, ToolExecutionDenied, and MCP approval ledger evidence.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemonization, hosted queues, worker fleets, and remote server operations.
external_adapter_responsibilities: MCP server implementation, GitHub/GitLab/Slack adapters, OAuth application wiring, and remote transport hosting.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: MCP-S5 should validate runtime MCP input and output data against a bounded schema subset before and after approved tools/call execution.
